A great wyrm hangs frozen mid-dive above the keep, its jaws yawning open as a torrent of white-gold fire cascades across the eastern battlements — stone glowing molten at the impact — while armored defenders scatter like ants along the parapet walk far below.

The siege gate buckles at the exact instant a dozen battering-ram crews heave in unison, iron-banded oak splintering inward in a fan of shards, while ten thousand infantry press behind scaling-ladders already cresting the curtain wall on every side.

A coronation ring of heralds and lords crowds the great stair as the sovereign kneels at its summit, the crown descending finger-width from the archbishop's hands, banners of every noble house snapping taut in sudden wind, the assembled host below reduced to a dense jeweled carpet.

Three catapults release simultaneously, their payloads — boulders wreathed in alchemist's fire — frozen mid-arc above the outer ward, trailing smoke contrails, while the defending garrison on the ramparts raises shields in a single collective motion, tiny as beetles against the castle's face.

A leyline-rift tears open directly above the keep's highest spire, a vertical wound of violet-white light wide enough to swallow the tower entire, its edges fraying into branching arcs that rake the surrounding walls while mages on the battlements brace against the shockwave.

A hundred longships round the sea-cliff headland simultaneously, every oar-bank lifted in the turning stroke, prows aimed at the sea-keep's harbor gate, while signal fires ignite along the castle's coastal wall and the garrison's tiny silhouettes flood the sea-facing ramparts.

The north tower's upper third hangs suspended in the precise instant before gravity claims it — a siege-engine stone buried in its face, cracks flowering outward in every direction — while soldiers on the adjacent wall sprint away and the courtyard below empties in a rushing tide of figures.

A mage-circle of seven robed figures stands atop the tallest tower, arms raised, a summoning storm forming directly overhead: a churning column of lightning and dark cloud anchored to their circle, its base no wider than the tower-top, its crown spreading across the entire sky above the castle.

Cavalry five thousand strong crests the ridge above the castle's approach road in a single surging wave, lances leveled, morning sun catching ten thousand points of steel simultaneously, while the siege army below the walls turns in fragmented panic, tiny figures scattering from the thundering line.

A blood-moon eclipse locks into totality directly above the castle, the moon's copper-red disc perfectly framed between the two highest towers, its ruddy light flooding every courtyard and wall-walk with arterial color while pilgrims pressed against the outer gate stare upward in a single frozen gesture.

A mounted host of a hundred knights thunders through the castle's barbican gate in tight formation, the leaders already in the courtyard as the rearmost clear the portcullis, hooves scattering cobblestones, pennants horizontal in the rush of passage, stable-hands and squires flattening against the ward walls.

The coronation processional crosses the great stone bridge at its midpoint — the carriage flanked by mounted household knights, the bridge crowded rail-to-rail with cheering subjects — while on the castle's grand stair ahead, the full court waits in ranked tiers, the open doors of the throne-hall blazing with torchlight.

A summoning portal blooms in the courtyard center, a disc of emerald and gold fifty feet across, its surface rippling like struck water, already showing a shadowed landscape beyond, while knights ring it with raised weapons and court mages at its perimeter strain against the vortex pulling at their robes.

Two dragons wheel in opposite directions above the keep simultaneously, one banking left across the gatehouse trailing a veil of smoke, one diving right toward the great hall roof, their wingspans bracketing the entire castle between them, defenders on every wall frozen mid-action in the shadow of both beasts.

An aurora-storm envelops the upper towers in cascading curtains of jade and silver light, the spires visible as dark silhouettes within the radiance, while on the outer walls sentries have abandoned their posts and pressed together in clusters, tiny dark figures watching the castle's pinnacles burn with cold fire.

A siege army of forty thousand fills the plain before the gates from tree-line to tree-line, their banners raised, ranked formations locked in final dress before the assault order, siege towers and catapults positioned — frozen in the last breath of stillness — while the castle's walls bristle with every defender it holds.

The sky-tear above the outer gate has opened wide enough to frame a sky of alien constellations beyond, its edges crawling with silver runes, and through it the vanguard of an armed host is mid-step across the threshold, armored figures emerging into the castle's world while the gatehouse garrison falls back.

A dragon lands on the gate-tower at the exact moment its forelimbs grip the parapet, wingbeats throwing men from the wall-walk in every direction, tail sweeping across the outer face of the tower, the portcullis chains snapping under the impact, the beast's head level with the tower's signal-fire beacon.

The breach in the outer wall erupts at its peak: a magical impact strike has punched through thirty feet of dressed stone, the rubble expanding outward in a frozen cone of shards, dust-cloud blooming beyond the walls while infantry on both sides — tiny against the gap — are mid-lurch in every direction.

The great army assembles on the muster-plain below the castle's landward face: banners of a hundred lords planted in ranked order, cavalry formed in wings left and right, pike-blocks filling the center, all in the last moment before the warlord's signal — the entire host stretched from castle-shadow to the distant forest edge.

A leyline-storm cracks apart the sky above the keep, six forking columns of white energy striking the six highest spires simultaneously, the towers' capstones glowing incandescent at each impact point, while every figure on every battlement — guards, mages, archers — is thrown flat by the concussive wave radiating outward.

Knights-to-be kneel in a double rank across the castle's inner courtyard, swords planted before each one, the lord-commander moving along the line with the accolade blade, frozen at the moment it touches the shoulder of the tenth candidate — while behind them the entire garrison and household pack the courtyard walls, watching.

A colossal wyrm hangs suspended above the gatehouse, jaw stretched wide, a column of white-hot fire mid-pour across the barbican's crown — the stone already glowing orange and crumbling at the edges. Tiny knights scatter along the wall-walk below, cloaks ablaze, too small against the vast scaled belly overhead to be anything but doomed.

The sky above the inner courtyard tears open in a blinding violet rift sixty feet across, its churning rim spitting arcs of raw leyline energy against the surrounding towers. Hundreds of pilgrims packed into the courtyard below recoil as one, their upturned faces no larger than coins against the howling aperture above.

Three siege towers have reached the eastern curtain wall simultaneously — the lead tower's drawbridge crashing down onto the battlements at this very instant, the first wave of scaling men spilling onto the parapet. Below, a battering ram the size of an oak swings at the gate, ropes taut, scores of soldiers straining at its handles.

The king stands on the topmost step of the great ceremonial stair, crown inches above his bowed head, the high-lord's hands trembling at the apex of the gesture. A thousand subjects fill the entire approach bridge and courtyard below, their collective roar frozen in the air, banners snapping rigid in the wind above the packed, tiny multitude.

A thousand mounted knights crest the ridge above the castle's approach road at full gallop, lances leveled, the front rank already thundering down the slope toward the besieged gatehouse. From the ramparts, defenders the size of insects watch the vast tide of horseflesh and steel break over the hillcrest like a wave.

A vast crimson wyrm hangs suspended mid-breath above the eastern gatehouse, a torrent of white-gold fire blooming against the stone, battlements exploding outward in frozen debris. Tiny armored defenders hurl themselves flat along the wall-walk, their shields raised uselessly against the inferno pouring across the ramparts.

An immense siege-ladder array crowds the northern curtain wall at full extension, hundreds of scaling men frozen one step from the parapet, while below a solid press of pike-and-shield infantry fills the killing-ground. Catapult arms stand at full release, boulders blurring mid-flight toward the barbican.

A leyline-rift tears the sky directly above the great keep's highest spire, the portal mouth ringed with spinning arcs of violet fire and grinding geometric light. Through the opening a shadow the size of a warship begins to emerge. In the courtyard below, tiny robed figures scramble outward from the epicenter.

The coronation processional has reached the apex of the grand outer stair, the crowned figure rising into full elevation before ten thousand subjects packed into the forecourt and along every battlement. Banners of every sworn house hang from every tower simultaneously, snapping rigid in the ceremonial wind.

Three war-dragons wheel in tight formation directly above the inner ward, one already descending with claws outstretched toward the drum-tower, two others banking in opposing arcs with fire trailing from their jaws. Soldiers on the wall-walk appear as scattered ants beneath the combined shadow.

The harbor sea-gate is choked from shore to shore with war-galleys, their oars raised vertical in the frozen moment of arrival, iron prow-rams gleaming, colored sails still full with wind. Along the castle's sea-wall every guard post is manned, tiny figures silhouetted against the massed fleet below.

A mage-circle of twelve practitioners stands on the highest tower-top, each figure outlined in searing white as the summoning sigil carved into the stone blazes to full ignition. A pillar of roiling storm-cloud descends directly onto the circle, lightning frozen mid-branch across every surrounding spire.

A vast cavalry host crests the ridge above the approach road at full gallop, lances leveled in an unbroken line stretching from treeline to treeline, their charge aimed directly at the open breach in the outer curtain wall. Inside the breach tiny defending infantry brace in locked-shield formation.

The great south tower is frozen mid-collapse, a cathedral's worth of masonry hanging impossible in the air, blown outward by a magical impact strike still blazing at the point of contact on the keep wall. Soldiers on the adjacent wall-walk are caught mid-leap away from the disintegrating parapet.

An armada of two hundred banner-flying war-galleys packs the sea-approach to the cliff-keep, their formation spreading from headland to headland, signal fires burning on every masthead. On the castle's harbor wall tiny sentinels stand motionless at the sight, the gate-portcullis half-lowered in the suspended instant.

A blood-moon eclipse hangs directly above the central spire, the sky around it stained deep amber and arterial red, auroral curtains of green and violet cascading down over every tower in frozen sheets. On the outer walls pilgrims and soldiers alike stand with faces tilted upward, tiny against the spectacle.

A battering-ram of blackened iron, carried by eighty men under a roofed siege-gallery, has struck the main gate at full momentum, the gate timbers frozen mid-explosion inward, iron brackets spinning outward. Defenders atop the gatehouse pour burning oil frozen mid-cascade, the liquid hanging like amber glass.

A sky-tear portal opens above the castle courtyard at its maximum diameter, wide enough to swallow the entire inner ward, its edges crackling with golden-white fire. Through it an army in formation is visible mid-crossing, the leading rank frozen one step above the cobblestones far below.

The great bridge approach is filled margin to margin with a royal procession, knights in full ceremonial plate flanking a golden carriage, the entire column stretching back beyond the gatehouse to the outer road. Every battlement above is crowded with tiny onlooking figures, pennants at full extension.

An ancient black wyrm has landed directly atop the gate-tower, one foreclaw crushing the parapet, its wingspan blotting the sky above the entire gatehouse complex. The portcullis chains are severed, frozen mid-snap. Tiny knights in the gateway tunnel below are caught in the act of scattering.

A massive host of assembled lords fills the entire plain before the castle gates, banners of a hundred houses arrayed in ordered blocks stretching to the horizon, every unit in formal muster formation. At the center of the formation a circle of mounted commanders faces the open castle gate.

A ritual circle etched across the full width of the courtyard blazes at simultaneous ignition, every carved line a conduit of blue-white fire, the assembled summoning mages at the circle's nodes thrown backward by the release. The castle's inner-ward towers frame the detonation, their windows blowing outward in frozen glass.

Dozens of catapult arms stand at full-release arc across the besieging army's lines, their payloads frozen at apex above the castle walls, a constellation of boulders, fire-pots, and chain-shot hanging motionless above the keep. The walls below show fresh craters, defenders caught mid-scatter at each breach-point.

A mounted knight-host fills the castle's main gate tunnel at full gallop, the leading riders emerging into the courtyard with lances dropping to horizontal, pennants streaming backward in the rush. The interior garrison is frozen mid-reaction, too small against the press of horsemen pouring through the arch.

A leyline-storm crowns the keep's highest spire, the vaulted cloud formation directly above it rotating around the single point of contact where visible energy flows down the stonework. Lightning strikes six surrounding towers simultaneously, frozen mid-bolt, the branching channels etched in blue fire against the night sky.

A fleet of longships rounds the sea-cliff headland in tight formation, oars churning identical white foam, iron shields lining every rail, the lead ship's prow aimed at the castle's sea-gate. On the cliff-top wall tiny defenders man the mangonels, arms hauled back at full tension.

Two great wyrms meet head-to-head directly above the castle's highest tower, their mutual fire-breath colliding in a blossoming sphere of orange and white at the apex, the shockwave frozen mid-expansion over the rooftops. On every battlement tiny soldiers are flattened by the pressure wave.

The investiture of a hundred knights proceeds simultaneously across the full width of the outer courtyard, every kneeling figure receiving the sword-touch in the same frozen instant, the presiding lord at the keep steps elevated above the scene. Banners of each new house drop simultaneously from the battlements above.

A wall section between the drum-tower and the gatehouse is frozen mid-eruption, a magical impact having struck dead-center, the outer face of the curtain wall peeling away in a slow-motion bloom of shattered ashlar. Behind the breach the inner ward is suddenly exposed, tiny soldiers visible in its depth.

A vast aurora-storm envelops all six towers simultaneously, cascading curtains of green-white-gold hanging from cloud to parapet in frozen vertical sheets, the entire castle silhouetted in relief against the spectacle. On the outer wall-walk a procession of pilgrims stands motionless, each figure a tiny dark mark against the overwhelming light.

A colossal wyrm hangs suspended mid-dive above the central keep, its jaws erupting a torrent of white fire across the battlements — the stone glowing molten orange. Tiny armored defenders scatter along the wall-walk, shields raised uselessly against the cascade. The entire gate-tower is silhouetted inside the inferno.

A portal the width of the courtyard tears open in absolute silence thirty feet above the flagstones — its edges bleeding violet lightning, its interior a churning void of pale gold light. Knights and stable-hands below are frozen mid-step, faces upturned, looking impossibly small beneath the blooming rift.

A thousand scaling-ladders clap against the outer curtain wall simultaneously — siege troops swarming upward like ants on bark while boulders from castle catapults arc outward trailing fire. The gate is ringed with battering-ram crews, and the plain beyond is an unbroken sea of enemy banners stretching to the horizon.

The new king stands at the apex of the great ceremonial stair, crown lifted by trembling hands of the High Lector, both figures dwarfed by the castle's towering facade. Below, the entire courtyard is packed — knights, lords, commoners — a living mosaic of colored banners, every face turned upward in perfect frozen awe.

A hundred mounted knights crest the ridge road in full charge, lances leveled, the castle's massive gatehouse looming directly ahead. The drawbridge is down and the portcullis rising — the lead rider's destrier is caught airborne mid-gallop, hooves clear of the earth, the thunder of the charge reaching the walls first.

Three robed figures form a triangle on the highest tower-top, arms raised, as a summoning sigil fifty feet across blazes white-hot between them. Arcs of raw magic crawl down the tower's outer stones toward the courtyard below where tiny soldiers press themselves flat against the walls in terrified reverence.

Forty war-galleys advance in tight formation into the harbor below the sea-keep, oars raised in unison at the peak of the stroke, banners snapping from every mast. The castle's sea-wall stretches above the harbor, its towers packed with defenders who look like pewter figurines against the vast stone face of the fortification.

A leyline-storm crowns the castle with a halo of crackling silver-white energy — bolts splitting downward along every spire and merlon simultaneously, the sky above bruised a deep violet. Pilgrims who had been crossing the bridge are frozen mid-stride, hair standing upright, their cloaks blown horizontal by the surge of raw arcane force.

Ten thousand soldiers stand ranked across the moonlit plain before the castle's main gate — banners of a hundred lesser lords planted in long rows, war-horses stamping, torches held aloft. The castle itself rises behind its own drawbridge like a cliff-face, its windows lit amber, dwarfing the entire gathered host that spreads to both horizons.

The northeast tower erupts outward from halfway up its height — a siege-stone impact frozen at the precise moment of maximum detonation, a crown of shattered granite and mortar suspended in the air. Tiny silhouettes of defenders are visible mid-fall along the wall-walk below, and a second stone is still visible arcing inbound.

Five dragons wheel in a loose spiral above the keep — the lowest one dragging its talons across the roof of the great hall, scattering flagstones like pebbles. Soldiers on the outer towers are reduced to specks against the wings of the circling wyrms, their crossbow bolts invisible threads lost in the smoke-dark sky.

A leyline-rift splits the castle's main gate in two vertical halves, tearing the iron-banded oak apart without touching it — raw silver light flooding the gatehouse passage from inside. A column of mounted knights approaching on the road outside have reined their horses to rearing panic, each animal and rider tiny against the gate's blazing frame.

Catapults along a mile-wide siege-line loose their payloads in one simultaneous volley — a hundred stones and clay fire-pots rising in a unified arc toward the castle's outer curtain wall. The tiny figures of engineers are still cranking winches as the first projectiles begin their descent, the wall's defenders bracing in a thin dark line.

A royal procession crosses the great stone bridge three abreast — gilded banners, white palfreys, heralds in blazoned tabards — the column stretching back out of the gatehouse and forward into the city below. The castle's twin gate-towers rise a hundred feet overhead, making the entire procession look like a ribbon of embroidery on a cliff-face.

A dragon-rider brings a copper-scaled wyrm to landing at the outer gate — the beast's wingspan casting the entire gatehouse in shadow, one foreclaw gripping the gate-tower's parapet and cracking the stone. Sentries on the tower top are dwarfed utterly, pressing against the merlons. The rider stands upright in the saddle at the apex of the wingbeat.

A summoning circle on the great courtyard flagstones — fifty yards across, carved lines now blazing gold — pulses at the moment its central pillar of light erupts upward through the open sky. Every person in the courtyard, knights and servants alike, is flung outward from the circle's edge, their tiny bodies suspended mid-air at the light's first apex.

An armada of war-galleys fills the sea-approach from cliff to cliff below the coastal fortress, their rams carving white foam, the lead ships already beneath the shadow of the sea-castle's barbican. Archers crowd the castle's harbor-wall battlements in a thin line, looking downward at a fleet that outnumbers every stone in the fortification.

A blood-moon hangs directly above the castle's highest spire — enormous, swollen, deep crimson — its light turning the entire fortress the color of old iron. A procession of pilgrims crossing the lower bridge below are reduced to a single dark thread of figures against the pale road, each one tiny beneath the castle's vast silhouette.

The outer curtain wall buckles outward at its center as a battering-ram of supernatural size — iron-headed, sixty feet long, carried by a hundred men — strikes the gate for what will clearly be its final blow. The wall-face has already begun to fracture in a starburst pattern, and tiny defenders on the wall-walk are mid-leap outward as the stone gives.

Three mages stand at the summit of the keep's crown-tower, a contained rift forming between their staffs — through it, a second sky is briefly visible, storm-green and alien. Lightning from the rift crawls downward along the tower's entire height. Below in the courtyard, every horse has bolted and every soldier is flat on the stones, arms over their heads.

A vast host of heavy cavalry crests the hill at the castle's flank — lances couched, pennants streaming — and the lead rank is already in the breach where the outer wall has been destroyed, the first horses mid-leap over the rubble. The castle's inner ward looms behind the breach like a cliff, its defenders small figures running to the sound of hooves.

The harbor below the sea-keep is so thick with longships that the water between them is invisible — mast-forests crowded from breakwater to breakwater, warriors standing packed on every deck, the lead ships already at the sea-gate's chain. The castle above is reflected in the harbor, its towers inverted in the water between the hulls of a hundred ships.

A winged great wyrm is frozen directly above the keep, every scale illuminated by the castle's own fires below, its fire-sac compressed at the instant before release — a sphere of orange pressure visible at its throat. On every battlement below, tiny archers have drawn but no arrow can reach. The shadow of the dragon covers the entire inner ward.

An aurora-storm erupts from the castle's tallest spire outward — curtains of green and white light folding across the sky in every direction from that single origin point above the tower-top. Soldiers garrisoning the wall-walk below have abandoned their posts to stare upward, their small figures leaning back on the battlements, faces lit in the cascading light.

The massive eastern gate-tower tilts — frozen at the precise moment its foundation gives way, the upper two-thirds of the tower leaning at an impossible angle, its stones separating mid-fall in a slow-motion curtain of masonry. Tiny soldiers are still on the wall-walk attached to it, and the siege-army below has stopped its advance to stare upward at the falling colossus.

A colossal wyrm hangs suspended mid-stroke above the eastern gatehouse, its jaws split wide, a column of white-orange fire rolling across the battlements in a solid wave. Tiny armored figures along the wall-walk are flung sideways by the blast-front. Stone crenellations explode outward in slow ruin.

The courtyard portal tears open at its widest — a circular rift thirty feet across, its rim crackling with violet fire, the interior a howling void of silver light. Robed figures in a ring below it are thrown to their knees by the pressure wave. The cobblestones directly beneath the rift glow white.

Ten thousand men fill the plain before the iron-banded gates, siege towers rolling forward on groaning axles, the lead tower's drawbridge just beginning to fall toward the parapet. Tiny knights on the walls hurl pitch. Catapult arms lash across the line simultaneously in a dozen arcing volleys.

The king stands at the apex of the great stair, the high priest's hands holding the crown at its apex — one inch above the bowed royal head — as the assembled court below fills every step and colonnade. A thousand banners drop in unison. The castle's bells are mid-toll, frozen in resonance.

A thousand heavy cavalry crest the ridge above the approach road simultaneously, pennants cracking forward in a single horizontal sheet, hooves still clear of the ground in mid-gallop, the castle gate-tower rising enormous and ancient behind them. Knights on the walls are specks against the banners flooding down the slope.

A mage-circle of seven stands on the summit of the highest tower, every sigil blazing gold, a pillar of conjured lightning rising from their joined hands straight up into a blackening sky. The tower-top stones crack outward from the heat. Soldiers on lower battlements press against the merlon-faces to shield their eyes.

Forty war-galleys packed shoulder to shoulder fill the harbor mouth, oars raised vertical in salute, their prows pointed at the sea-castle's harbor chain. The lead galley's ram is a foot from the chain's central link. Tiny dock-guards scramble along the breakwater. The castle's harbor-tower looms above the mast-forests.

A vast leyline-storm crowns the keep — three intersecting arcs of white fire spanning the full width of the tower, the sky above them split into alternating bands of bruised purple and searing gold. The spire at the summit glows through its stone. Sentries on the upper walkway cling to the merlons.

The great siege-ram swings at its absolute furthest back-arc, its iron wolf's-head gleaming, fifty men gripping the chains, the castle's main gate directly before it. The gate's outer timbers already show a splintered crater from the previous blow. A carpet of fallen soldiers lies small and still before the threshold.

A dragon the color of tarnished copper has landed on the gate-tower's crown, its full weight pressing the stones, wings half-spread for balance. The tower noticeably leans. Tiny defenders on the adjoining wall-walk are sprinting away. A single crossbowman stands frozen mid-aim directly below the creature's descending neck.

The sky above the keep tears open in a vertical rift four spire-heights tall, its edges peeling back like burning parchment to reveal a luminous amber void. Through the rift, enormous armored shapes are mid-step crossing the threshold. Pilgrims in the outer courtyard below scatter in every direction, tiny as ants.

Scaling ladders crowd every inch of the western curtain wall, thousands of soldiers mid-climb, the topmost men one arm-reach from the battlements, the defenders leaning out with pole-arms, the whole castle wall alive with the frozen moment of first contact. Battering-ram crews are specks at the base.

The royal procession crosses the great drawbridge at its midpoint, the mounted king beneath a canopy of gold, the bridge so packed with knights and heralds that figures spill onto the gatehouse roof above. Crowds on the bank and outer walls are a smear of color and upraised hands. The portcullis is full-raised.

Three dragons wheel simultaneously above the castle's highest towers, each at a different altitude, their wing-beats producing a visible pressure-shockwave in the clouds above the keep. Soldiers below in the inner ward are flattened against walls and pillars. One dragon's tail sweeps through the upper spire, stone fragments mid-arc.

A summoning circle erupts on the inner ward's flagstones, its lines scorched a foot deep, the figure rising from its center already twice the height of the surrounding walls. Robed summoners at the circle's edge are flung radially outward, mid-air. Guards at the ward's four corners are tiny silhouettes against the light.

The northern tower collapses at its midpoint, a horizontal ring of exploding masonry frozen in its outward flight, the upper half of the tower still intact and suspended above the fracture for this one instant. Siege-engine crews on the plain below are specks. Defenders on the adjacent wall-walk dive mid-fall.

A hundred lords' banners fill the plain before the castle in perfect ranked lines, a host so vast the furthest rank blurs into the treeline. Heralds on horseback ride the front line, tiny. The castle gates stand open, the king visible on the great stair as a single bright speck in full regalia.

A fleet of longships rows in formation toward the sea-keep's water-gate, the lead ship's dragon-prow reaching the gate's chain, the oars of all ships raised mid-stroke in frozen unison. Tiny archers crowd the sea-wall's parapet above. The keep's harbor-tower blocks the sky behind the mast-tops.

The mage on the keep's southern rampart releases a working at full discharge, a horizontal blade of shearing force catching the siege-tower mid-body, the tower's upper section mid-tilt and mid-dissolve, timbers flying. Tiny soldiers on the ground scatter from beneath the falling debris-cloud. The castle's wall stands firm and bright behind the destruction.

A cavalry host of riders with lowered lances charges through the breach in the outer wall, the broken masonry still mid-fall on both sides, the riders' mounts leaping rubble at full gallop. The inner gate-tower fills the sky before them. Defending footmen are a thin ragged line in the gateway throat.

The blood-moon eclipse reaches totality directly above the castle's central spire, the moon a perfect crimson ring around a core of absolute black, its light turning every battlement and tower the color of cooling iron. Tiny monks kneel in rows in the outer ward. The eclipse shadow is a perfect circle around the keep.

A vast armada fills the estuary before the river-castle wall-to-wall from bank to bank, the lead war-galleys already inside the harbor chain, their towers packed with archers. The castle's riverside wall is a solid line of defenders, tiny in the aggregate. Catapults on the battlements are frozen mid-launch.

Seven simultaneous catapult strikes hit the castle's outer curtain wall at once, each impact mid-explosion, stone and mortar erupting outward in seven separate blossoms of ruin along the wall's length. The assault army on the plain below is a solid black carpet of figures. The inner keep rises untouched behind the broken curtain.

A rift-portal opens at the exact center of the great hall's ceiling, its circumference wider than the hall itself, the portal's rim tearing through the upper masonry. Through it pours a cascade of silver-armored figures in mid-fall. Guards and courtiers at floor level are scattered figures, arms raised, faces upturned.

The investiture knight kneels on the courtyard flagstones, the sovereign's blade at the exact point of touching his shoulder, the full chivalric court ranked in horseshoe formation around them. Every banner in the courtyard is full-extended in a single gust. Tiny squires and heralds line every gallery and staircase above.

A colossal wyrm hangs suspended above the central keep, jaws split wide, a torrent of white-hot fire erupting across the battlements in a roaring cascade — the stone glowing cherry-red, crenellations blasting apart mid-flight. Along the scorched wall-walk, tiny armored figures scatter and dive, silhouetted against the inferno.

The great harbor churns as a hundred war-galleys arrive in tight formation, oars raised in unison, their bronze rams gleaming below the sea-castle's cliffside walls. Every dock and rampart bristles with tiny watchmen; the leading vessel's crimson prow-banner snaps taut in the salt wind at the apex of the fleet's arrival.

The coronation stair of the high citadel blazes with torchlight as the crowned figure lifts the scepter overhead at the topmost step — the crowd below, filling the vast courtyard in a dense human carpet of tiny upturned faces, erupts in a single roaring cheer, banners surging like a breaking wave across the cobblestones.

A siege tower has just kissed the outer wall at the moment the drawbridge slams down across it — a tide of armored infantry pouring across, while below the gate catapults loose in perfect unison, five great stones arcing simultaneously through smoky air toward the curtain wall. Tiny defenders jam the battlements, spears leveled.

An enormous leyline-rift tears open directly above the inner courtyard, the sky splitting like parchment from horizon to keep-top in a blaze of silver-white light. Through the widening gash, geometric lattices of raw magic flare outward, crackling down the spires. Below, pilgrims and soldiers drop to their knees in the courtyard, impossibly small beneath the rupture.

A thousand cavalry crest the ridge overlooking the castle's approach road simultaneously — the front rank already driving lances horizontal, the ground shaking as the charge avalanches downhill toward the open gate at full gallop. From the walls, tiny sentinels stare outward at the churning sea of banners and horseflesh descending upon them.

Three great dragons wheel in tight formation above the keep's tallest spire, banking hard at the apex of their turn — wingspans overlapping, the downwash raking the tower-top flags horizontal. On the battlements far below, tiny crossbowmen tilt their weapons skyward in helpless arcs, their bolts vanishing into the vast shadow cast by the wheeling wings.

On the flat summit of the highest tower, a ring of seven mages stands frozen at the peak of the summoning — arms flung outward, robes blasting in the conjured gale, a pillar of violet fire erupting straight up from the sigil-carved stone between them. Far below on the outer walls, tiny sentries shield their eyes against the glare.

The northern curtain wall detonates outward mid-collapse — a sixty-foot section of ancient masonry erupting in a cloud of dust and tumbling blocks, the breach yawning open at its widest instant. A siege-engine bolt is still visibly embedded in the crumbling core. Along adjacent wall-walks, tiny soldiers are caught in mid-sprint away from the catastrophic failure.

An armada fills the sea-castle's harbor to the outermost breakwater — flagship at the fore, its massive sail dropping at the exact moment the anchor chain runs, forty vessels in perfect echelon behind it. The quayside and every rampart above are lined with tiny figures, the collective roar of welcome and warning indistinguishable from this height.

The sky above the keep cracks open in a blood-moon eclipse — the moon swollen and crimson, locked precisely at totality, cathedral rays of deep-red light stabbing down through cathedral-cloud breaks to ignite the highest spires in carmine fire. On every tower and wall-walk, tiny figures stand motionless, staring upward in collective dread at the blood-drenched sky.

A battering ram the size of a felled oak swings at the apex of its arc — iron dragon-head aimed at the gate's center, the ram-crew of a hundred men leaning back on the chains in perfect unison. Above the gate arch, tiny defenders tip boiling pitch from stone cauldrons in a gleaming cascade frozen mid-fall through torchlit air.

The vast royal procession fills the bridge spanning the castle moat from end to end — knights in polished plate flanking a gilded carriage at the precise midpoint, banners of forty houses snapping overhead. On the towers flanking the gate, tiny trumpeters lean out over the parapets, instruments raised, the brass note hanging in the still morning air.

Scaling ladders cover an entire quarter-mile section of the outer wall — hundreds of them, each with figures climbing in silhouette against the firelit sky, the topmost attackers and the topmost defenders clashing at the wall's edge simultaneously across the whole face. Siege-fire arcs overhead; the moment is the wall's entire length alive with combat at every merlon.

A massive summoning sigil, a hundred feet across, blazes to full illumination across the cobblestones of the inner courtyard — each carved line igniting gold in sequence until the whole geometric form burns at once. The castle walls loom on all four sides, dwarfing the robed figures at each node of the circle, their shadows thrown long and sharp by the sudden blaze.

A dragon-rider's mount descends in a near-vertical dive toward the gatehouse, wings folding back at the last instant — clawed feet extended, the great body blocking the entire gate-tower from view. Below, tiny stable-hands and gate-guards fling themselves flat against the cobblestones as the displaced air hammers outward in a visible shockwave ring across the courtyard.

The host has assembled — every approach road, every field before the castle gates black with ranked formations, banners of a hundred lords planted in regimental blocks stretching to the horizon. The gates themselves stand open, and the tiny figure of the commander on horseback faces the assembled mass from the threshold, dwarfed absolutely by the gathered army behind.

A portal blooms above the keep's great hall roof — perfectly circular, fifty feet across, its inner surface showing a landscape of iron mountains in a copper sky, the rim crackling with white chain-lightning. Through it, the vanguard of an armored host is visible mid-stride. On the parapets below, tiny archers stand frozen, arrows half-drawn, staring upward.

Five catapults on the siege-line loose in the same heartbeat — five projectiles at the apex of their trajectories simultaneously above the outer wall, the closest stone a split second from impact with the gatehouse tower. The wall's defenders are tiny panicked figures scrambling beneath. Below, the catapult crews are already hauling windlasses for the next volley.

A Rohirrim-styled cavalry tide pours through the collapsed eastern gate in a single churning torrent — a thousand horses compressed into the breach, the lead riders already inside the outer ward, lances splintering against defenders. The gate arch frames the flood; beyond it, tiny defenders form a desperate shield-wall across the courtyard, half-swallowed by the oncoming mass.

Leyline-storm lightning clusters above every spire simultaneously — fifteen towers lit by branching bolts at once, the energy cascading down iron weathervanes and exploding the flagstones of the outer parapet in geysers of sparks. The castle's full silhouette is outlined in white fire against a black sky. Tiny figures on the curtain walls have flattened themselves to stone.

The great wyrm's underbelly slides over the gatehouse at rooftop height — the beast's full length bisecting the castle's skyline, wingbeats hammering the inner courtyard flat. Tiny soldiers beneath it cling to wall-rings and archway columns. The dragon's tail demolishes a turret in a spray of masonry frozen mid-explosion while the enormous head already clears the far wall.

A knight-investiture fills the central courtyard at its solemn apex — the high lord's sword extended flat above the kneeling candidate's shoulder, a hundred assembled knights in full heraldic plate ranked in concentric arcs around them. The castle's four towers rise on every side, dwarfing the ceremony; on the wall-walks above, tiny heralds raise trumpets in unison.

A sky-tear rips open diagonally across the face of the keep itself — not above it but through its visible facade, reality peeling back along a jagged seam from the base of the great tower to the crenellation line, the inside of the tear blazing with gold-white dimensional fire. Tiny figures on the courtyard below freeze in absolute stillness.

Longships fill the channel below the sea-castle's cliff-face walls — hulls grinding together in the packed approach, shields ranked along every rail, warriors in iron-banded helms standing at the prows. Above them the castle's sea-gate is mid-opening — the portcullis chain taut at its highest point — while tiny archers crowd every arrow-slit in the cliffside curtain wall.

A colossal wyrm hangs frozen mid-breath above the eastern gatehouse, a solid column of white-fire pouring down the curtain wall, battlements glowing molten orange. Tiny armored figures on the ramparts are caught mid-flee, their cloaks exploding backward in the heat-blast, dwarfed entirely beneath the dragon's chest.

The great summoning-portal tears open directly above the inner courtyard, a churning disc of jade and violet light three times the keep's height, its rim shedding arcs of crackling energy onto the cobblestones below. Pilgrim figures scatter across the yard like scattered seeds, impossibly small beneath its howling mouth.

Ten thousand infantry press against the outer gate in a single cresting wave, siege-towers grinding forward on each flank, scaling-ladders bristling along the full length of the western curtain wall. Defenders are mere specks at the parapet, overwhelmed and dwarfed by the sheer black mass of the assault.

The king stands motionless on the highest step of the great ceremonial stair, crown descending from the high priest's hands at the exact instant a thousand torches ignite across every balcony and battlement. The assembled court and crowd fill the courtyard below like a sea of upturned faces, tiny as scattered grain.

A hundred armored knights crest the ridge road at full gallop, lances leveled, pennants snapping horizontal, the entire host compressing into a single gleaming wedge aimed at the shattered castle gate. The castle's towers loom enormous behind the breach; riders are mere glinting slivers against its stone immensity.

Three mages stand inside a blazing sigil-circle chalked on the highest tower-top, arms raised, as a column of crackling storm-light erupts upward from the circle into the roiling clouds. Lightning answers in a downward cascade around the spire; soldiers on the lower battlements below look like insects beside the eruption.

An armada of war-galleys stretches from horizon to harbor mouth, every oar lifted simultaneously at the stroke-master's beat, colored war-banners filling the scene with a forest of poles. The sea-castle's walls rise sheer from the harbor rocks; the nearest galleys are half its height, the rear fleet mere painted specks.

The northern tower gives way at mid-height, a catastrophic bloom of shattered masonry frozen in the air like a stone flower mid-opening, a siege-engine bolt still visible at the point of impact. Defenders on the adjacent wall section are tiny figures diving, fragments the size of houses spiraling outward past them.

A leyline-storm crowns the keep in a halo of branching violet fire, great arcing tendrils of raw magical current coiling around every spire and turret simultaneously, the sky above curdled into a bruised spiral. Sentinels on the wall-walk are silhouetted and tiny inside the light, their cloaks trailing upward in the energy-wind.

The portcullis buckles inward as the iron-shod battering-ram drives home, a shockwave of splinters and chain erupting in both directions through the gatehouse tunnel. The ram-crew beneath their timber shell is a small dark shape against the gate's immensity; on the walls above, archers are reduced to matchstick figures in the chaos.

A coronation procession crosses the great drawbridge in full ceremonial order, heralds, knights, banner-bearers and robed clerics stretching back to the far bank, the lead riders already entering the gate arch. The castle's twin gate-towers dwarf the entire column; the procession is a thin bright ribbon threading through stone giants.

A leyline-rift splits the air at the main gate itself, a vertical tear of blinding silver light from cobblestone to cloud-base, its edges peeling back to reveal a churning void of golden geometry beyond. Gate-guards press back against the walls to either side, tiny armored figures shielding their eyes from the impossible light.

Two great dragons wheel in opposing spirals above the central keep, a third dropping in a near-vertical stoop toward the great hall roof, claws extended, wingspan blotting the sun from the courtyard below. Crossbowmen on every turret are barely visible specks raising their weapons toward the circling forms overhead.

A host of ten thousand assembles on the plain before the castle in perfect martial order, banners of forty lords standing rigid in the wind, ranked cavalry on the flanks, pike-blocks filling the center. The castle gate and walls behind them are vast and silent; the entire army barely reaches the height of the curtain wall.

The harbor of the sea-keep is packed edge to edge with longships, their prows locked together in the press, shields lining every gunwale, torchlight reflecting in a continuous blaze off the black water. The castle headland rises behind the harbor, enormous and impassive, the fleet below it dense as fish-scales and half as large.

A ritual circle of seven mages on the courtyard floor blazes with white light, and from its center a titan's arm of condensed fire reaches upward toward the overcast sky, punching through the cloud-layer. Knights ringing the courtyard walls are tiny silhouettes pressed against the stonework, shielding their faces from the ascending column.

The crown prince's triumph-parade floods through the open gate in a torrent of cavalry, cheering footmen, and fluttering standards, the column wide enough to fill the full gate-passage and still banking to either side. The gate-towers overhead are colossal; the procession spills from beneath them like water from a dam-crack.

A dragon lands on the left gate-tower at the exact moment of contact, claws seizing stone, one wing still fully extended over the outer ward, the impact-shockwave radiating in a visible ring of displaced dust. A handful of soldiers on the tower-top are caught directly beneath the descending claw, utterly dwarfed.

Catapults behind the siege-lines have loosed simultaneously; twelve boulders are frozen mid-arc above the castle's outer wall, their trajectories drawn in converging lines toward the keep. Siege crews are specks beside their massive machines; the entire castle facade faces the incoming volley, its windows and ramparts alive with tiny defending figures.

A blood-moon eclipse crests directly above the keep's highest spire, its rust-red disc framed perfectly in a break in the cathedral-clouds, god-rays of crimson light pouring straight down onto the courtyard and upper walls. Pilgrims gathered below in the courtyard are barely visible, raised hands like tiny splinters reaching toward the light.

A mounted host rounds the final bend of the approach road and charges across the open ground toward the castle's outer gate at full gallop, the ground trembling visibly in the frozen moment, a dust-cloud surging behind. The gate is enormous and still shut; the cavalry wedge is a gleaming dart aimed at its heart.

A wall-section thirty yards wide erupts outward in a single catastrophic burst, a siege-mine having detonated beneath it, a hemisphere of fire and broken masonry frozen in perfect expansion. The breach is wide enough to march an army through; the nearest scaling-party soldiers are tiny silhouettes inside the eruption's outer edge.

A vast portal tears open above the keep's central tower, and through its gaping mouth the leading edge of an armed host is visible mid-crossing, the first mounted knights and banners already emerging into the castle's sky. Gate-soldiers below on the walls look upward, reduced to specks by the portal's enormous churning circumference.
